title: Arrays, shapes, copies and views
outcome: Trace array storage and indexing while choosing deliberately between copies and shared views.

exercises.title: Read a shape
exercises.task: Compare a length 2 vector with a2-by -1 matrix.
exercises.hint: Element count does not determine the number of axes.
exercises.answer: Operations can dispatch or broadcast differently for these shapes.

exercises.title: Trace column order
exercises.task: Locate value 5 in the reshaped matrix.
exercises.hint: Follow columns through the input vector.
exercises.answer: The storage order is explicit and should not be confused with the scientific interpretation of axes.

exercises.title: Take a snapshot
exercises.task: Mutate an ordinary slice from a vector.
exercises.expected: The original scalar-element vector is unchanged.
exercises.answer: A snapshot protects later reads from this mutation, with an allocation cost.

exercises.title: Use a shared window
exercises.task: Mutate a view of the same range.
exercises.hint: A view refers to existing storage.
exercises.answer: A view is useful when shared mutation or avoided copying is intended.

exercises.title: Copy nested state
exercises.task: Compare copy and deepcopy on a vector of vectors.
exercises.expected: A shallow copy shares inner vectors; a deep copy does not in this fixture.
exercises.hint: Inspect both outer and inner identities.
exercises.answer: The required independence level depends on the data structure and algorithm.

exercises.title: Retain a bound check
exercises.task: Read index 0 from a standard two-element vector.
exercises.hint: The valid standard indices start at 1.
exercises.answer: Bounds checking makes a violated indexing contract observable before considering lower-level optimizations.
